articles.title: Judi Dench has inspired a new decorating trend – and I oppose it with every fibre of my being
articles.summary: Reverse decluttering is here, prompting a shudder from me and my fellow neat freaks. Why would you want to be surrounded by mementos when you could be perfectly tidy? Older doesn’t always mean wiser. Jo Whiley has spoken about a home hack she picked up from – clang!
body: Whiley went to interview Dench for her RHS Roots podcast and found the actor’s house “packed with family photographs, children’s drawings and memories everywhere”. Mind-blowingly, she means this as a positive. “Seeing Judi’s reminded me that lived-in spaces are often the most beautiful because they reflect a lifetime of love, family and shared experiences,” she says. “I suddenly thought: ‘Why am I putting all these things away?’” As soon as I got home, I immediately put all the family photographs back out.” TLDR: I cleaned up and then I made it all messy again. Shudder.

He has a mustard cravat that also smells like mustard, despite many spins in the washing machine, which belonged to a great-great-aunt’s husband’s brother. You’d be amazed how few occasions call for a cravat, unless you assumed it was none at all. My husband is like a bird refusing to budge from its nest because it’s fiercely protecting eggs, but instead of eggs it’s nonfunctional laptops, antique T-shirts and a pungent cravat.
points: Reverse decluttering is here, prompting a shudder from me and my fellow neat freaks.
Why would you want to be surrounded by mementos when you could be perfectly tidy?

articles.title: Swimmers warned of toxic algae at newly designated Thames bathing site
articles.summary: People told they and their pets should keep out of river at Ham amid anger over Thames Water’s treated sewage plan. Swimmers are being warned not to enter the water at the first official bathing site on the River Thames, in south-west London, because of toxic blue-green algae in the water.
body: The blue-green algal blooms are rare in moving water but are likely to be caused by the extreme heat, low river flow, and nutrient pollution from sewage waste.
Thames Water’s Hogsmill sewage treatment plant, in Kingston upon Thames, is situated three miles upstream of the Ham bathing site.

Marlene Lawrence, of the swimming group Teddington Bluetits, which successfully applied for the bathing water designation at Ham, said: “This is so unusual to get blue-green algae in a moving body of water. It is the first time in nearly six years of swimming here that this has happened.
“The river is very low-flowing at the moment because of the lack of rain and the high temperatures we are having. With climate change, this is likely to happen more.”

articles.title: Matthew Higham obituary
articles.summary: My former partner and friend Matthew Higham, who has died aged 79, lived a cheerfully chequered life: running away from London to Scotland as a teenager to marry his pregnant first wife, Kay, when their parents forbade it; training as a blacksmith and at the E15 theatre school in London, alongside…
body: Having driven trucks to various parts of the world, in 1978 he co-founded, with his brother Ben, St Giles European Transport, a specialist antiques haulage company in Norwich, and afterwards became an antiques dealer in the city.

Restless by nature, Matthew’s antique hunting gave him licence to roam across Europe, and later the US and China, finding worn and weathered treasures in remote places. Along the way he collected many experiences and stories, which he recounted with delight to anyone who would listen. Over the years he also accumulated two wives, two partners and five children.

Born in Holborn, central London, to David, a literary agent, and Helen (nee Witton), a journalist, Matthew grew up in Hampstead, north London. He attended various schools in the area, but none of them recognised his dyslexia, and he survived by becoming the class entertainer. Largely self-educated, in his teens he became politically aware, joined at least one Aldermaston march, and left the Sea Scouts to briefly hook up with the Communist Party of Great Britain.

articles.title: Why Anthony Bourdain’s Editor Wanted ‘Tony’ to Be Darker
articles.summary: There are two types of biopics: those that unconventionally show, and those that exhaustively tell. Thank goodness that Tony, the highly anticipated A24 biopic about the late Anthony Bourdain, takes the former route.
body: Eater spoke with the film’s screenwriters about casting the titular role, chef cameos, and more BTS moments.

Then again, successfully pitching a Bourdain biopic to his estate was always going to be a big swing. I spoke with Todd Bartels and Lou Howe about what made that swing possible (for one: bringing on Kimberly Witherspoon, Bourdain’s literary agent and friend, as an executive producer); which cast member demonstrated the best culinary chops; and who they could imagine playing an older, more seasoned Anthony Bourdain.
Eater: How did you strike the balance between making a movie for the passionate Anthony Bourdain fans, and viewers who may know very little about him?

Lou Howe: I was anxious about that [ laughs ], especially at the very beginning. But [we] just [tried] to make a good movie, and hope that the entertainment factor and emotional engagement hits the target well enough. We started this whole process as fans, so in that way we felt relatively comfortable servicing fellow fans. You want to write a good story that people can plug into no matter who the character is. Of course, there are some Kitchen Confidential Easter eggs.
points: There are two types of biopics: those that unconventionally show, and those that exhaustively tell.

articles.title: Your Meal Times Might Be Giving You “Metabolic Jet Lag”
articles.summary: You meal times can affect metabolism, sleep, and blood sugar. Experts explain how to avoid "metabolic jet lag" with a consistent eating schedule.
body: Such are the pleasures of vacation—and life. However, this kind of seasonal hedonism can leave your body feeling super out of sync. You know the vibe: puffy, bloated, sluggish, and generally feeling icky.

“These changes can lead to temporary imbalances,” corroborates Samia Rhalem, a dietitian at Royal Mansour Tamuda Bay. “Some people may notice weight gain or an increase in body fat, while others experience unstable blood sugar levels, elevated cholesterol or triglycerides, digestive discomfort, or simply lower energy because their diet has become less nutrient-dense.”
Luckily, this is all usually temporary. Returning to a balanced diet often helps—and so does something else: simply eating at regular times.
Like sleep, our appetite follows a circadian rhythm. This internal “master clock” in the brain helps coordinate everything from hormone production to digestion, and responds primarily to light.

articles.title: Tanya Ravichandran Is the Collector Obsessed With McQueen and Ann Demeulemeester
articles.summary: Tanya Ravichandran owns over 200 Demeulemeester and 400 McQueen pieces. “I always make a joke that I like the hunt more than the actual pieces of clothing.”
body: Every morning, before coffee or working out, the New York-based photographer and content creator Tanya Ravichandran starts her day by scrolling through a bevy of resale sites. “I wake up, go on my phone, and immediately check every single secondhand app’s listings,” she says. It may sound like a shopping compulsion, but Ravichandran has a crystal-clear focus: She is always on the hunt for vintage items from Alexander McQueen and Ann Demeulemeester. “I have a bot that scours the entire internet twenty-four seven. I don’t miss a single thing.”
Wearing an Alexander McQueen top and skirt (both from spring 1999), Alexander McQueen shoes (from 2022), and vintage gloves.

While her (mostly black-and-white) closet is filled with other labels such as Margiela and Tom Ford-era Gucci, Ravichandran’s focus on Demeulemeester and McQueen has made her collection extremely unique. So, why the fascination around those two designers in particular?
points: Tanya Ravichandran owns over 200 Demeulemeester and 400 McQueen pieces.

articles.title: 7 All-Inclusive Resorts in the US That Are Worth the Splurge
articles.summary: From a Montana cattle ranch to a Sedona canyon retreat, these American resorts prove the US can do all-in-one vacations just as well as the tropics.
body: I love piecing a trip together myself, mapping out every restaurant reservation and day trip until the itinerary is exactly right. But over the years—and especially since becoming a mom —I've come to appreciate what an all-inclusive resort takes off my plate. These properties fold your room, meals, drinks, and often your activities into one upfront rate, so you're not doing math over a glass of wine or budgeting out an afternoon of kayaking. You know your total cost before you land, and you get to actually be present with your family instead of managing a running tab and a packed schedule.
Included in the rate: Three farm-to-table meals daily, afternoon tea, guided hikes, an indoor pool, boating, golf, and most outdoor activities; alcohol and spa treatments cost extra.

Why we love it: This Victorian-era castle sits on its own lake and comes with 85 miles of hiking trails and a nine-hole golf course—all folded into the nightly rate. It's also one of the more accessible drives on this list, about 90 miles from New York City, so it's an easy sell for a long weekend without a flight.
points: From a Montana cattle ranch to a Sedona canyon retreat, these American resorts prove the US can do all-in-one vacations just as well as the tropics.

articles.title: The Best Fresh Perfumes Go With Everything
articles.summary: Bright, breezy, and never overpowering, the best fresh perfumes by Dior, Byredo, and more are effortless scents that work for practically any mood or occasion.
body: If there’s a fragrance for every mood, personality, and occasion, the best fresh perfumes are all-encompassing. “A fresh and clean perfume is like an open window or a deep breath of morning air,” Delphine Jelk, Guerlain’s Creative Director of Fragrance, tells Vogue. “It’s never flat—it has texture, light, and a sense of movement.”

Jeniece Trizzino, VP of Innovation & Product at Scentbird and Drift, agrees, adding that fresh scents are less about smelling like particular notes, and more about the feeling they evoke. “There’s a lightness and clarity to these scents that feels almost restorative,” Trizzino says. And while these scents can certainly be airy and intimate, she emphasizes that they also hold a quiet confidence. “They don’t need to announce themselves to be memorable,” she adds.

articles.title: Adam Baidawi and Alex Marxsen’s New York Wedding Was a Love Letter to Their New Home City
articles.summary: GQ’s global editorial director Adam Baidawi married the Lululemon marketing executive Alex Marxsen in a whirlwind New York City Hall wedding that included pizza slices, shooting hoops, martinis at Bemelmans Bar, and just two guests.
body: Adam Baidawi and Alex Marxsen’s love story spans well over a decade and unfolded across four continents. Adam, the global editorial director of GQ, first met Alex, who works in global marketing for Lululemon, in their hometown of Melbourne, Australia, in 2014. “I was 21, and Adam was a few years older,” Alex remembers. “We were both still living with our parents in the suburbs, and I think I’d been abroad twice… and yet somehow, the relationship became more international than we ever could have imagined.”

Two months after they met through mutual friends as they began falling in love, Alex left Melbourne for a long-planned study abroad exchange program. “I thought I’d made the biggest mistake leaving Adam and this new relationship,” she adds. “I was beside myself for weeks but quietly hopeful we’d find our way back to each other. Adam was attempting to play the cool and indifferent older guy, but eventually cracked and flew over to meet me in the States after I wrapped my exchange program. We then took a wild trip from Madrid to Marrakech to Los Angeles, and have been together ever since.”

articles.title: Amazon Is Making Alexa+ Free for These TVs
articles.summary: We may earn a commission from links on this page. It's 2026, which means every tech company needs to have its own AI service—often available as a subscription, of course. For Amazon, that's Alexa+, which officially rolled out earlier this year.
body: That's now changing, depending on your TV. Amazon announced on Wednesday a new initiative to roll out Alexa+ for free for compatible Fire TV devices. The company says that millions of customers are already using Alexa+ on their Fire TVs, and while it doesn't specify, my guess is the vast majority of those are Prime users. It seems Amazon is trying to fill the gaps in its user base here, by offering Alexa+ to Prime-less Fire TV users.

Amazon says that Alexa+ delivers a "smarter, more conversational voice experience" than its original Alexa assistant. Alexa+ is designed to understand context better than the previous iteration, which means it should be able to respond to more detailed, complex questions. In addition, Amazon says the assistant remembers your preferences, and returns more relevant recommendations.

While Alexa+ works with entertainment, it's still a smart home assistant, too. You can ask Alexa+ to move a show or movie to another Fire TV in your house, access live camera feeds from your security system, run scenes and routines, control individual smart devices, check the weather, and set timers.
